title: Adaptive micro-batching thresholds and backpressure for high QPS
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Under sustained high QPS for short-form generation endpoints we observe increased tail latency and occasional OOMs on serving GPUs. Root cause investigation indicates two interacting factors: (1) continuous micro-batching accumulates many small requests into large micro-batches which cause transient GPU memory spikes when combined with large KV caches; (2) the current static micro-batch thresholds and fixed max_wait_ms do not adapt to changing QPS, seq-length distributions, or GPU memory pressure, leading to either excessive latency (waiting for batch fill) or dangerous memory oversubscription.

Goal: Implement an adaptive micro-batching and backpressure mechanism that dynamically tunes per-model micro-batch size and wait thresholds in response to observed QPS, latency SLOs, and GPU memory usage. The system should: maintain P95 latency SLOs, avoid GPU OOMs, provide graceful degradation under overload (soft shedding + rate-limit signals), and coordinate with KV cache policies to reclaim headroom predictably.
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive micro-batching algorithm deployed to canary pool for model family 'm-compact' with runtime telemetry enabled
Under synthetic sustained 10k QPS generated by loadtest, P95 generation latency increases by <= 20% vs baseline while reducing GPU OOMs to zero over 30m run
Cluster-level metric 'microbatch.adaptive.size' reported per-queue and per-GPU and tracked in console dashboards
Backpressure signals (HTTP 429 + Retry-After) emitted for >2% of requests for controlled overloads and customers see documented SDK retry guidance
KV cache evictions triggered proportionally when GPU memory > 82% and logs show ordered eviction events with reason='adaptive-backpressure'
implementation_plan: Design: introduce a controller that computes target_batch_size and max_wait_ms per model-queue using EWMA of QPS and service latency (latency_headroom = SLO - EWMA(latency))

Memory safety: compute estimated_memory_per_batch = batch_size * model_mem_per_token * avg_seq_len + kv_cache_reserved; reserve safety_margin (default 15%) and cap batch_size so estimated memory < gpu_safe_threshold (e.g., 85%)

Backpressure policy: two-stage response — soft internal throttling (reduce batch acceptance and prioritize short requests), then external shedding (HTTP 429 with Retry-After) once queue length or memory exceeds thresholds
KV coordination: when memory pressure detected, trigger KV cache partial eviction policy that evicts least-recently-used shards proportional to required headroom instead of full flush

Implementation tasks: controller service (runtime), scheduler integration (serving runtime batching loop), metrics plumbing, config flags (min_batch, max_batch, smoothing_tau), tests and canary rollout
Engineering milestones: unit tests -> integration tests with load-gen -> canary rollout -> ramp to 25% -> evaluate -> full rollout
testing_plan: Load tests: synthetic load generating variable QPS (1k-20k) and variable seq lengths to validate stability and auto-scaling of batch size
Chaos tests: inject KV cache pressure by preloading KV entries to simulate cold-start heavy sessions and verify proportional eviction
Regression tests: ensure no change in correctness of generation outputs and that function-calling and streaming remain compatible
Canary: deploy to dedicated canary GPUs with tracing enabled; run 2h sustained ramp and 30m peak bursts
Performance benchmarks: compare token/sec, P95/P99 latency and GPU memory curves vs current static thresholds
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-model adaptive batching panel and per-GPU memory/safety margin plot
Alerts: fire if adaptive.memory_headroom < 5% for >2m or OOM rate >0 in last 10m
SLO observability: automated regression alert if P95 latency increases >25% vs baseline after rollout
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: oscillation of batch size causing jittery latency. Mitigation: use EWMA smoothing and hysteresis windows before applying increases/decreases
Risk: aggressive KV eviction may hurt cache hit rates and increase total token compute. Mitigation: proportional eviction and prefer evicting cold shards; add per-customer cache limits
Risk: SDK clients mis-handle 429. Mitigation: publish SDK retry helpers and short Retry-After guidelines; use graceful degradation priority lanes for enterprise customers
Risk: estimation mismatch for memory per token across quantized kernels. Mitigation: conservative per-model memory lookup table; fallback to safe single-request processing when uncertainty high

2026-03-05 Natasha Kim (SRE): Reviewed memory safety calc — suggested adding a hard cap guard that forces single-request fallback for any per-batch estimate > 90% of GPU capacity. SRE flagged need for alerting on kv_eviction_rate.
2026-03-08 Design review: Alex Gomez requested UX field for 'customer_priority' so we can prefer high-priority lanes in soft-throttle. Added to next iteration.
2026-03-10 Marco Ruiz: Canary deployed to 'canary-us-west' pool at 10% traffic. Observed adaptive.batch_size median 4 -> 8 during ramp, memory headroom stable ~12%. No OOMs during 1h stress.
Follow-ups: schedule post-mortem after 72h canary and confirm SDK docs update.
